records.query: Need the histopathological biopsy report of the sinonasal mass to definitively confirm or exclude malignancy, and the MRI evaluation for perineural or intracranial invasion, as these are core findings for staging and treatment planning.
records.text: - Microscopic examination: Diffuse large atypical plasmacytic infiltrate. Tumor cells were large, with round eccentric nuclei, vesicular chromatin, single prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, abundant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, and occasional atypical mitoses.    - Immunohistochemical stains: Tumor cells positive for CD38, CD138, CD56, MUM-1 with λ immunoglobulin light chain restriction and strong positive for EBER. Ki-67: 30-40%. Negative for CD45, CD3, CD5, CD20, PAX-5, CD30, cytokeratin, and S100.

bindings.label: Patient presented with left-sided nasal obstruction for 1 year
Patient is in their 40s with a medical history of sleep apnea and diabetes, no history of immunosuppression, and negative serum HIV test results
Bilateral nasal endoscopy revealed an excised mass with an aggregated size up to 7.0 cm in its greatest dimension
Histopathology shows diffuse large atypical plasmacytic infiltrate with CD138, MUM-1, lambda restriction, and EBER positivity
MRI shows an infiltrating sinonasal mass with hard palate erosion
Immunophenotype excludes carcinoma and B-cell lymphoma
The sinonasal mass is plasmablastic lymphoma
Bone marrow biopsy is negative for involvement
The sinonasal mass is plasmablastic lymphoma
The sinonasal mass is B-cell lymphoma
Staging PET-CT and serum markers are unavailable
The plasmablastic lymphoma is localized to the sinonasal region
